title: Chronic liver disease
summary: Chronic liver disease meeting one of: hemorrhaging from varices/portal hypertensive gastropathy, ascites/hydrothorax, hepatorenal syndrome, hepatopulmonary syndrome, hepatic encephalopathy, or end-stage liver disease (high MELD).

children.criterion: Hemorrhaging from esophageal, gastric, or ectopic varices or portal hypertensive gastropathy with hemodynamic instability requiring transfusion of at least 2 units of blood
Ascites or hydrothorax not attributable to other causes, present despite continuing treatment
Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) with peritoneal fluid containing absolute neutrophil count of at least 250 cells/mm³
Hepatorenal syndrome documented by elevated serum creatinine, oliguria, and absence of other causes of renal failure
Hepatopulmonary syndrome documented by arterial hypoxemia and intrapulmonary vascular dilatations
Hepatic encephalopathy documented by altered mental status with elevated ammonia or asterixis
End-stage liver disease with MELD score of 22 or greater on at least 2 evaluations within a 6-month period
